title: Dedicated Structured-XOR Solver for Even-Mansour
summary: For four or more rounds, strong zero-bit structure remains unexploited, leaving open a dedicated solver with competitive time-memory trade-offs.

formal_statement.body: For $r\ge 4$, design a dedicated solver for the structured $(r+1)$-XOR instance of $r\mathrm{EM}$ with competitive $(T,M)$ trade-offs.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of the Even-Mansour construction using structured XOR instances.
parameters: r: round count, restricted to four or more
scope.unresolved_remainder: Design a dedicated solver for the structured (r+1)-XOR instance of r-round Even-Mansour with competitive time-memory trade-offs.

citations.label: Low-Memory Attacks Against Two-Round Even-Mansour Using the 3-XOR Problem

progress.summary: The source explicitly opens this question after observing strong structure in the lists, including many bits fixed to zero. It asks for a dedicated algorithm with competitive computational time and memory trade-offs.
citation_labels: Gaëtan Leurent et al., Low-Memory Attacks Against Two-Round Even-Mansour Using the 3-XOR Problem
